name: Oxiracetam
lead: Oxiracetam is a synthetic nootropic of the racetam family, related to piracetam. People take it for focus, memory and mental clarity, and its looks relevance is indirect: better concentration and recall can support consistent study, work and training routines.[1]

It has been used as a prescription medicine for cognitive impairment in some countries, and it has been tested in randomized trials in vascular cognitive impairment, post-stroke cognitive decline and traumatic brain injury.[2][3][4] Laboratory work links racetams to cholinergic and glutamate (AMPA receptor) systems, though no single mechanism is agreed.[5][6]

quick.overview:
Oxiracetam is a racetam, a class of cognition-oriented compounds related to piracetam. It was developed in the 1970s-80s and has been marketed in some European and Asian countries for cognitive impairment.

In communities focused on self-improvement, it is used as a nootropic aimed at focus, memory and learning, supporting the study and work that sit behind a lot of ascension routines.
quick.mechanism: Racetams are reported to modulate AMPA-type glutamate receptors and cholinergic activity, and oxiracetam has been studied for effects on acetylcholine in animals. Reviews note that no commonly accepted single mechanism has been established.
quick.risks: Reviews of the piracetam-like nootropics describe very low toxicity and few serious side effects; headache is the effect most often mentioned. It is a prescription drug in some countries and is not approved by the US FDA.

paras: Oxiracetam has no direct effect on appearance that sources describe. Users describe it as a focus and memory aid that helps them keep up study, work and training.
It has been prescribed in some countries for cognitive impairment associated with degenerative or vascular dementia, and post-stroke recovery.[1][7]

Reviews of racetams report reversal of experimentally induced amnesia in animals, evidence of cholinergic interaction, and positive modulation of AMPA-sensitive glutamate receptors in neuronal cultures, with no single accepted mechanism.[5][6][8][9]

A double-blind randomized trial in organic brain syndrome and a controlled trial in Alzheimer disease were published in 1987 and 1992.[10][11] A multicenter placebo-controlled phase IV trial examined oxiracetam in vascular cognitive impairment.[12] A Korean multicenter trial examined oxiracetam, with physical activity, for preventing cognitive decline after stroke.[13] A multicentre phase 3 trial in China tested L-oxiracetam and oxiracetam against placebo for cognition after traumatic brain injury.[14] Oxiracetam appeared among 21 drugs in a network meta-analysis of vascular dementia treatments.[15] A 2026 phase 1 registration studies IQ-test reliability under racetam-class compounds in healthy people.[16]
Reviews describe the piracetam-like nootropics as having very low toxicity and lacking serious side effects.[5]
